name: Prayer And Fasting
overview: Scripture presents prayer and fasting as powerful spiritual disciplines that demonstrate dependence on God and a desire for His guidance, as seen when Moses fasted forty days and nights without food or water while receiving the Ten Commandments (Exodus 34:28). Fasting is portrayed as a means to humble oneself before God, seek His direction, and intercede for others, exemplified by Ezra's fast to seek a right way for his people (Ezra 8:21) and Nehemiah’s mourning and fasting in prayer (Nehemiah 1:4). Esther’s call for a three-day fast before approaching the king highlights fasting as preparation for courageous obedience (Esther 4:16). Moreover, Isaiah reveals that true fasting involves not only abstaining from food but also pursuing justice and mercy by breaking the bonds of wickedness and freeing the oppressed (Isaiah 58:6). Daniel’s example of abstaining from pleasant food and anointing for three weeks (Daniel 10:3) further underscores fasting as a form of spiritual discipline and self-denial.
